anchors.description: Front-face width of the black side-by-side refrigerator, between its left and right vertical front-door edges at mid-height (both doors plus the center seam visible).
anchors.visible_evidence: Freestanding side-by-side refrigerator seen almost frontally: two black doors with a center seam, in-door ice/water dispenser on the left door; both endpoints lie on the left and right vertical front-face edges at the same image row, so the 3D segment lies in the door plane.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Exact model unknown; 36 in (0.914 m) is the dominant US side-by-side width, with 33 in and 42-48 in built-ins possible, hence the +/-5-8% interval.

anchors.description: Depth of the kitchen countertop on the right wall, from the open countertop front edge back to the counter/backsplash junction at the wall, along the same image column clear of appliances.
anchors.visible_evidence: Light stone countertop visible as a continuous bright band between the beige tiled backsplash and the dark shadow line of the front edge; the column x=530 is free of the kettle and the white canister, so both the front edge and the wall junction are directly visible.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Standard US base-cabinet counter depth is 24-25.5 in (0.61-0.65 m) including overhang; the surface is seen at a grazing angle, so a 1-2 px endpoint error maps to roughly 0.03 m.
